description: The band CASE uses @days < 30 for '0-29' and BETWEEN 31 AND 60 for '31-60'. A claim with exactly 30 days since last activity matches neither and gets 'UNKNOWN'. days_since_activity is never negative (reported_date <= AsOfDate and payment_date <= AsOfDate), so 30 is the only value that reaches UNKNOWN.

impact.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_rpt_claim_aging WHERE days_since_activity = 30 OR aging_band = 'UNKNOWN'

impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_rpt_claim_aging WHERE days_since_activity = 30 OR aging_band = 'UNKNOWN'
intended_behaviour: The bands should cover every value with no gaps: 0-29, 30-60, 61+ (or 0-30, 31-60, 61+). Day 30 should get a real band, not UNKNOWN.
title: Ageing band gap: 30 days falls into UNKNOWN

description: weeks_open = DATEDIFF(WEEK, @reported, @AsOfDate). This counts the Sunday week boundaries crossed, not completed 7-day weeks, so a claim reported on a Saturday shows 1 week open the next day and the result can be one week off from the real elapsed weeks.

impact.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(weeks_open - CAST(FLOOR(DATEDIFF(as_of_date, reported_date) / 7) AS INT))), 0) AS amount_affected FROM golden_rpt_claim_aging WHERE weeks_open <> CAST(FLOOR(DATEDIFF(as_of_date, reported_date) / 7) AS INT)

impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(weeks_open - CAST(FLOOR(DATEDIFF(as_of_date, reported_date) / 7) AS INT))), 0) AS amount_affected FROM golden_rpt_claim_aging WHERE weeks_open <> CAST(FLOOR(DATEDIFF(as_of_date, reported_date) / 7) AS INT)
intended_behaviour: Whole weeks the claim has been open, i.e. FLOOR(DATEDIFF(DAY, reported_date, AsOfDate) / 7).
title: weeks_open counts week boundaries, not elapsed weeks

description: The cursor builds the total with SET @total = @total + @amount. If any payment up to the reporting date has a NULL amount, the running total becomes NULL and stays NULL, so total_paid is NULL for the whole claim even though its other payments have amounts. The NULL-amount payment is still counted in n_payments.

impact.query: WITH p AS (SELECT claim_id, SUM(amount) AS amt, SUM(CASE WHEN amount IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_null FROM stg_claim_payments WHERE payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' GROUP BY claim_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(COALESCE(p.amt, 0))), 0) AS amount_affected FROM golden_rpt_claim_aging g JOIN p ON p.claim_id = g.claim_id WHERE p.n_null > 0

impact_query: WITH p AS (SELECT claim_id, SUM(amount) AS amt, SUM(CASE WHEN amount IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_null FROM stg_claim_payments WHERE payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' GROUP BY claim_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(COALESCE(p.amt, 0))), 0) AS amount_affected FROM golden_rpt_claim_aging g JOIN p ON p.claim_id = g.claim_id WHERE p.n_null > 0
intended_behaviour: NULL amounts should be ignored (as SUM does), so total_paid is the sum of the known payment amounts.
title: A NULL payment amount makes total_paid NULL

description: Payments are copied from stg.claim_payments without removing duplicates (staging has a _row_seq column, which suggests a payment can be loaded more than once). If a payment_id appears more than once for a claim, every copy is added to n_payments and total_paid.

impact.query: WITH d AS (SELECT claim_id, payment_id, COUNT(*) AS c, MAX(amount) AS amt FROM stg_claim_payments WHERE payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' GROUP BY claim_id, payment_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1), per AS (SELECT claim_id, SUM((c - 1) * COALESCE(amt, 0)) AS extra FROM d GROUP BY claim_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(per.extra)), 0) AS amount_affected FROM golden_rpt_claim_aging g JOIN per ON per.claim_id = g.claim_id

impact_query: WITH d AS (SELECT claim_id, payment_id, COUNT(*) AS c, MAX(amount) AS amt FROM stg_claim_payments WHERE payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' GROUP BY claim_id, payment_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1), per AS (SELECT claim_id, SUM((c - 1) * COALESCE(amt, 0)) AS extra FROM d GROUP BY claim_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(per.extra)), 0) AS amount_affected FROM golden_rpt_claim_aging g JOIN per ON per.claim_id = g.claim_id
intended_behaviour: Each payment (claim_id, payment_id) should be counted once.
title: Duplicate staged payment rows are double-counted
